title: Films, Stories & Independent Practice
subtitle: Build film vocabulary, follow a story and practise known grammar independently.

units.title: Film Language & Story
units.tagline: Describe characters, plots and ideas in a film.
notes: A plot is the sequence of events in a film or story.
A character is a person in the story; the main character is especially important.
Use adjectives to describe a film: funny, exciting, surprising, sad or inspiring.
A good story often has a problem, a development and an ending.

vocabulary.meaning: the story and events in a film
vocabulary.example: The plot became more exciting near the end.

vocabulary.meaning: a person in a film or story
vocabulary.example: The main character made a brave choice.
My favourite scene was at the train station.

vocabulary.meaning: the final part of a story
vocabulary.example: The ending was surprising but hopeful.

vocabulary.meaning: achieving good results or becoming popular
vocabulary.example: The film was successful because people recommended it.

vocabulary.meaning: to grow or change over time
vocabulary.example: The story developed slowly in the first half.

grammar.title: Review: Past Simple for a film story
grammar.rule: Bir filmi veya geçen hafta izlediğin bir şeyi anlatırken Past Simple kullan. Düzenli fiillere -ed gelir; düzensiz fiiller ikinci hâl alır.
examples: I watched a comedy on Saturday.
The friends went home at the end.

units.remember: Film hakkında konuşurken 'The film was...' ile genel fikrini, 'The character did...' ile olayları anlatabilirsin.
units.watchOut: Bir hikâyeyi geçmişte anlatırken 'The hero find...' değil, 'The hero found...' kullan.

reading.title: A Film with a Small Idea
reading.text: A young filmmaker named Elif wanted to make a film about a lost bicycle. Her friends thought the idea was too simple, but Elif developed the story carefully. In the first scene, a boy found an old key in the bicycle basket. Then he met people from different parts of his town and learned why the bicycle mattered to them. The ending was quiet: he returned the bicycle to its owner, who had used it when she was a child. The film did not have famous actors, but audiences liked its warm characters and clear story.

questions.prompt: Where did the boy find the key?
Why did audiences like the film?
options: It had warm characters and a clear story.
The bicycle went to a new town.

listening.title: Choosing a Film Idea
listening.script: Mert: I want to make a short film for our school project. Aylin: What is your idea? Mert: It is about two friends who find an old camera. Every photo shows a place from the past. Aylin: That sounds interesting. What is the problem in the story? Mert: They disagree about who should keep the camera, but finally they give it to the town museum. Aylin: Good ending. You can make the characters very different from each other.

questions.prompt: What do the two friends find?

options: They disagree about keeping the camera.

questions.prompt: Where do they give the camera?

units.title: Independent Grammar & Film Writing
units.tagline: Use familiar grammar accurately while planning a short review.
notes: Review questions and negatives with Past Simple: Did you like it? I didn't like the ending.
Review countable and uncountable nouns in a film-night context: many films, much time, a lot of popcorn.
Use a few linked sentences to explain your opinion: I liked it because..., but..., so....

grammar.title: Past Simple questions and negatives
grammar.rule: Did/didn't sonrasında fiilin yalın hâli gelir. Bu yapı, daha önce öğrenilen geçmiş zaman tekrarını kendi başına çözmek için kullanışlıdır.

grammar.title: Many, much and a lot of
grammar.rule: Many sayılabilen çoğul isimlerle; much sayılamayan isimlerle kullanılır. A lot of ikisiyle de kullanılabilir.
examples: They bought a lot of popcorn.

units.remember: Kendi kendine çalışırken önce soruyu oku, sonra ipucunu kullan ve sonunda cevabı kontrol et. Amaç puan değil, hangi yapıyı tekrar edeceğini görmek.
units.watchOut: Did ile soru sorarken ikinci hâl kullanma: 'Did the story began?' değil, 'Did the story begin?'.

writing.prompt: Write 8–10 sentences about a film you like. Say what kind of film it is, introduce one character, explain the basic plot without giving every detail, and give your opinion.
support: My favourite film is ... It is a ...

speaking.title: Say Your Film Pitch
speaking.prompt: Imagine you are planning a short film. Speak for one minute: name the main character, describe the problem, say where the story happens and give it an ending.

reading.title: Why a Good Film Works
reading.text: A good film does not need a complicated plot. It needs characters that the audience can understand and a clear reason to keep watching. At the beginning, viewers should learn who the main character is and what that person wants. Then the story needs a problem. The character can make mistakes, change plans or ask for help. Near the end, the problem should become clearer. A strong ending does not always mean a happy ending, but it should feel connected to the earlier scenes.

questions.prompt: What should viewers learn at the beginning?
options: Who the main character is and what they want

questions.prompt: What does a story need after the beginning?
Does a strong ending always have to be happy?
options: No, but it should connect to earlier scenes.
